summary: Moon Base Fire Map plots 273 fire tests from the International Space Station (NASA's FLEX droplet-burning experiment) by oxygen level and air pressure, right next to the air planned for a Moon base (at least 30% oxygen, at most 10.2 psi). It shows at a glance that no past test was run in exactly those conditions, and how close the nearest ones came.
details:
What it does: Moon Base Fire Map plots 273 fire tests from the International Space Station (NASA's FLEX droplet-burning experiment) by oxygen level and air pressure, next to the air planned for a Moon base (at least 30% oxygen, at most 10.2 psi). It shows that no past test was run in exactly those conditions, and how close the nearest ones came.

How it works: A short Python script reads NASA's public FLEX data table, removes one row with a missing pressure value, converts pressure to psi, and counts the tests in each region. 3 rows were compared by hand against the raw file. Results: 0 tests at 30% oxygen or more and 10.2 psi or less. The 17 closest tests used 30-34% oxygen at 10.33-10.50 psi, and 15 of those 17 ended in "Disruption". For comparison, 43 of the 249 tests below 30% oxygen ended in "Disruption".

Who it helps: Moon base air is planned to have more oxygen than Earth air, and more oxygen makes things burn more easily. The map helps students and the public see the gap, and helps mission designers see which planned conditions go beyond what past tests covered.

Limits: These are small fuel droplets (methanol, heptane), not cabin fires. What "Disruption" means in the data is not confirmed. Only 24 tests were at 30% oxygen or more. The "Disruption" comparison is not like-for-like: none of the 24 high-oxygen tests added the extra gases that many lower-oxygen tests used, and fuels and setups differ, so it does not show that oxygen caused "Disruption". It covers one experiment (FLEX); other ISS fire experiments were not checked.

What is different: Instead of just listing experiments, it puts past tests side by side with a stated future condition, so the untested gap is obvious.

Tools: Python 3 standard library; plain HTML and JavaScript, no outside libraries. Code licence: Apache-2.0. Code: https://github.com/JLFinance25/moon-base-fire-map. Not endorsed by NASA.

AI tools: Claude (an AI assistant) wrote most of the code, the web page and the slides.
